items.headline: OpenAI Rolls Out a Teen-Only Version of ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens on August 18, a separate experience for 13-to-17-year-olds with content restrictions around topics like self-harm, no romantic or flirty chat responses, and a new "Study Mode" that guides kids toward figuring out answers instead of just handing them over. Anyone the system thinks might be under 18 gets automatically placed into it.
items.why_it_matters: If you have teens at home, or your audience does, this is worth knowing about since it changes what ChatGPT will and won't do for that age group, and it's a good excuse to check the parental controls now rather than after a problem comes up.

items.headline: DaVinci Resolve 20.2 Adds an AI Fog Effect and Long-Awaited ProRes RAW Support
items.summary: Blackmagic's DaVinci Resolve 20.2 update brings a new AI Cinematic Haze tool that adds realistic atmospheric fog to a shot using an AI-generated depth map (with sliders to control how far it reaches and how strong it looks), plus native support for Apple ProRes RAW footage and a faster surface tracker.
items.why_it_matters: If you edit in Resolve, you can now add a moody fog or haze look to a flat shot without a plugin, and if you shoot on a camera that records ProRes RAW, you can finally bring that footage in natively instead of converting it first.

opportunity.action_note: Update to DaVinci Resolve 20.2 and try the new AI Cinematic Haze tool on a recent project so you can show it off in your next Resolve tutorial.

items.headline: YouTube Changes How It Recommends Membership Prices Outside the U.S.
items.summary: Starting August 19, YouTube updated the price recommendations it gives creators for channel memberships sold outside the United States, factoring in what audiences in each country can actually afford rather than just the exchange rate. Existing members keep their current price, and members paying in U.S. dollars aren't affected.
items.why_it_matters: If you sell channel memberships and have viewers outside the U.S., check YouTube Studio, your suggested pricing for new international members may have shifted, and you can always accept, tweak, or override the recommendation yourself.

opportunity.action_note: If you offer channel memberships, open YouTube Studio's membership pricing page and review the new recommended international prices before accepting them by default.
